params.system:
You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

   1| # W1-GEN — STATEMENT (target statement)
   2| 
   3| Ticket W1-GEN, Theory Wave 1. Lead: Claude Opus 5.5.
   4| Status of this file: **v2.3** (v2 LOCKED 2026-11-08; v2.1 (C6) design, v2.2 (C1′) added, v2.3 (C5)(d) layout and (C1′) energy — all logged in LOG.md) after statement-lock review R01 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol high,
   5| LOCK-WITH-CHANGES; all nine required changes applied, see `reviews/R01_statement_lock_sol.md` and its disposition
   6| `reviews/R01_disposition.md`). Later changes are logged in LOG.md and flagged in REPORT.md.
   7| 
   8| SoP = `Theory_work/State_of_Project/sections/`; NBH = `Theory_work/Old_Projects/New_BVS_Headquarters/`;
   9| BS = `NBH/branch_snapshots/`; T22iii = `Docs/Theory/proofs/T22iii_T16_start_aggregation/`.
  10| 
  11| ## 0. Target and how this statement answers it
  12| 
  13| Goal (HQ brief): consistency of the method's **reported** HPM Ŝ⁺ on a general, checkable class of correlated designs,
  14| p ≤ n^A (A > 1 allowed), masking allowed, of the form "on 𝒟(...), P(𝒪 ∩ {Ŝ⁺ ≠ S₀}) → 0", with LH, W, LH-iid as
  15| instances. Starting point, M5(0) (SoP `04_theory.tex:464-539`, T38-(0) "PROVED (SF: VERIFIED (W3-VT38E); XF:
  16| VERIFIED* (A-REV5))"), at every n and any X:
  17| 
  18|   P(𝒪 ∩ {Ŝ⁺ ≠ S₀}) ≤ 2E₀[1 − π(S₀)] + D_n,   D_n := P(𝒪̄ ∩ {S₀ ∉ 𝒮̄⁺})  (potential-run notation).     (M5-0)
  19| 
  20| S-T (TH09, T03♯) gives 1 − π(S₀) → 0 in probability, hence E₀[1 − π(S₀)] → 0 (bounded convergence). **The new
  21| content: a general design class on which D_n → 0.** This is a sufficient class, substantially narrower than "any
  22| correlated design" (CE169; non-identifiable designs; see §4).
  23| 
  24| ## 1. Setting
  25| 
  26| * **D0** as in SoP `04_theory.tex:69-74`: shipped g = n score, a₀ = b₀ = 0.01, normalized capped BB(1,p) prior,
  27|   K = min(p, ⌊n/2⌋), Ω = {S : |S| ≤ K}, tables r_b(U) = m(U)/m(∅), start γ₀ ∝ w(|S|)∏_b r_b(S ∩ C_b) on Ω, π₀,
  28|   start mode S̃₀ = argmax_Ω γ₀ with the size-then-lex tie rule.
  29| * **G**: fixed raw design X^r (n × p, nonconstant columns), y^r = α1 + X^rβ + ε, ε ~ N_n(0, σ²I), σ² > 0 fixed;
  30|   X = CX^rD_x⁻¹ (‖x_j‖² = n − 1), μ := CX^rβ = Xθ*, θ* := D_xβ, S₀ := supp β, s₀ := |S₀| ≥ 1 fixed, p = p_n ≤ n^A
  31|   (A ≥ 1 fixed; p ≫ n allowed).
  32| * **Notation.** P_T: projection on span X_T; Λ_T := ‖(I − P_T)μ‖²; Δ_T := Λ_T/(n − 1); v_T := σ² + Δ_T;
  33|   R̂_T := X_TᵀX_T/(n − 1); θ*_min := min_{j∈S₀}|θ*_j|. For a pair (T, l), l ∉ T, **only on the families named below,
  34|   where the relevant SE guarantees (I − P_T)x_l ≠ 0**: u_{T,l} := (I − P_T)x_l/‖(I − P_T)x_l‖, δ_{T,l} := u_{T,l}ᵀμ,
  35|   so that Λ_T − Λ_{T∪{l}} = δ²_{T,l}. For T with λ_min(R̂_{T∪{l}}) = 0 we use the projection form
  36|   Λ_T − Λ_{T∪{l}} (always defined).
  37| * **Blocks** C₁, …, C_J: the method's actual partition (complete linkage on 1 − |r̂|, top-down cut at B, next-fit
  38|   packing; B = min(⌊√n⌋, ⌊√p⌋, 16)), SoP `02_method.tex:187-211`; under G a deterministic function of X.
  39| * **Method:** v3.1 with LS0 as specified (SoP `02_method.tex:490-506`); local search M §6.10 (SoP `02_method.tex:463-467`);
  40|   cap ℓ_n = ⌈log₂(n + p + 1)⌉. A *move* is a strict improvement to the best scanned neighbour (lexicographic ties);
  41|   every scanned neighbour is scored; after ℓ moves one further scan; the LS0 centre is emitted (scored).
  42| * **Implementation premises** (named, not proved here; M5's list, SoP `04_theory.tex:86`): EX-A, EX-S, CAL, SR,
  43|   GUARD-W, OP-LS0, **e4** (emitted LS0 centre = the prescribed start-mode maximiser; DP invariant N3 OPEN, owned by
  44|   W1-N3), complete scans; for R′ > 4 also IND-T and the extra search from c₄ (nested scored set).
  45| 
  46| ## 2. Hypotheses
  47| 
  48| **(H0) = the hypotheses of S-T/T03♯** (SoP `04_theory.tex` TH09 card, from NBH TLF:448-451), written out:
  49| * R1: fixed s₀ ≥ 1, p ≤ n^A, s₀ ≤ K eventually; G;
  50| * R: ‖μ‖² ≤ Mn for a fixed M; λ_min(R̂_{S₀}) ≥ φ₀² for a fixed φ₀ > 0;
  51| * SE_λ(j₀), j₀ := ⌈(2A + 1)s₀⌉ + 1: λ_min(R̂_{S₀∪J}) ≥ φ₀² for every J with |J| ≤ j₀ (normalized);
  52| * SE_w(m♯_n; g₀): λ_min(X_{S₀∪J}ᵀX_{S₀∪J}) ≥ g₀ for every |J| ≤ m♯_n (unnormalized; fixed g₀ > 0), where
  53|   m♯_n := min{m ≥ s₀ : R_m ≤ n^{−(s₀+2)/2}}, R_m := Σ_{k=max(m+1,0)}^{K} C(p,k) w(k)/w(s₀) (deterministic, data-free);
  54| * BM-∞: θ*²_min n φ₀²/(σ² log n) → ∞. (BM(c > c₀) is not used.)
  55| 
  56| **(H1) Bounded, separated relevance set (descent).** Deterministic sets 𝒱_n ⊇ S₀ with |𝒱_n| ≤ v̄ (fixed) such that
  57| * (H1a) SE on 𝒱: λ_min(R̂_{𝒱∪{l}}) ≥ φ₀² for every l ∈ [p];
  58| * (H1b) SEP(c_S): ζ_n := max{Λ_S − Λ_{S∪{l}} : S ⊆ 𝒱, l ∉ 𝒱} ≤ c_S (n − 1) φ₀⁴ θ*²_min eventually, for a fixed
  59|   c_S ∈ [0, 1). Convention: ζ_n := 0 if 𝒱 = [p].
  60|   Variables outside 𝒱 may be correlated among themselves (subject only to (H0)'s anchored sparse-eigenvalue
  61|   conditions and (H2a)); they only must not carry, given any subset of
  62|   𝒱, more partial signal than the fixed fraction c_S of the guaranteed best-truth decrement (n − 1)φ₀⁴θ*²_min.
  63| 
  64| **(H2) Centre (on the actual blocks).** A deterministic reference S* ⊆ 𝒱 (S* ∈ Ω, s* := |S*| ≤ v̄,
  65| U*_b := S* ∩ C_b) such that
  66| * (H2a) within-block SE: λ_min(R̂_T) ≥ φ₀² for every nonempty T ⊆ C_b, every b;
  67| * (H2b) VIS(S*): for a deterministic M_n → ∞, g_{b,U} := ‖(P_{U∪U*_b} − P_U)μ‖² ≥ M_n v_U log n for every b and every
  68|   U ⊆ C_b with U*_b ⊄ U;
  69| * (H2c) NL(S*): with the leakage family 𝓛(S*) := {(b, T, l) : l ∈ C_b ∖ U*_b, U*_b ⊆ T ⊆ C_b ∖ {l}},
  70|   (i) δ²_{T,l} ≤ C_L σ² log n on 𝓛(S*) for a fixed C_L < ∞, and
  71|   (ii) NL_avg(κ) for a fixed κ > 0: if p > s*, eventually
  72|   (p − s*)⁻¹ Σ_{l∉S*} max_{T:(b(l),T,l)∈𝓛(S*)} exp(E_{T,l}) ≤ n^{1/2−κ}, where, for a fixed ε₀ > 0 and
  73|   h_n := √(2(A + ε₀) log n), E_{T,l} := min{δ²_{T,l}/(2Δ_T), δ²_{T,l}/(2v_T) + |δ_{T,l}|σh_n/v_T}, with E_{T,l} := 0
  74|   when δ_{T,l} = 0 (in particular when Δ_T = 0); the average is omitted when p = s*.
  75|   (NL_η(S*): δ²_{T,l} ≤ ησ² log n on 𝓛(S*) with 0 ≤ η < (√(2A+1) − √(2A))², implies (i) and (ii), as in T22iii §2.)
  76| 
  77| S* is an **existential certificate** depending on (X, β, σ², partition): it is not required to be the exact minimiser
  78| of Λ in each block (exact minimisers can contain nulls with negligible gain and violate VIS; R01 item 2). Masking is
  79| allowed: true variables with no block-level signal given U*_b are omitted from S* (they lie in 𝓛(S*)), and S* may
  80| contain nulls (block-level proxies).
  81| 
  82| ## 3. Claims
  83| 
  84| **(C1) Centre law (generalized T22(iii)).** [G, R (bounded energy only), p ≤ n^A, (H2), s* ≤ v̄]: 1 − π₀(S*) → 0 in
  85| probability; on {π₀(S*) > ½} the maximiser of γ₀ is unique, so S̃₀ = S*; hence P(S̃₀ = S*) → 1. The proof re-runs
  86| the locked T22(iii) argument (reference S₀) with reference S*, with (H2c) in place of NL_η, and with EXP′ **proved**
  87| (uniform score expansion, L1) instead of assumed.
  88| 
  89| **(C1′) Canonical certificate (added after R05, v2.2; sufficient condition for (H2b)–(H2c), no hypothesis changed).**
  90| Under (H2a), let γ_b be the coefficients of the projection of μ on span X_{C_b} (the regression of μ on the block's own
  91| columns). Assume also ‖μ‖² ≤ Mn. If every γ_b = γ^L_b + γ^S_b (disjoint supports) with, for a fixed
  92| η ∈ [0, (√(2A+1) − √(2A))²) and some M_n → ∞, (i) ‖X_{C_b}γ^S_b‖² ≤ ησ² log n and (ii)
  93| √((n − 1)φ₀²)·min_{j∈supp γ^L_b}|γ^L_{b,j}| ≥ √(ησ² log n) + √(M_n(σ² + 2M) log n) whenever supp γ^L_b ≠ ∅,
  94| then S* := ∪_b supp γ^L_b

   1| # L2 — Centre law with a general reference S* (generalized T22(iii)); claim (C1)
   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)**; lemma check R03 (Codex Sol): VERIFIED-WITH-AMENDMENTS, amendments
   4| applied (v2, reviews/R02_R04_disposition.md).
   5| Inputs: T22(i) "PROVED-LOCKED" (`Docs/Theory/proofs/T22_T16_start_aggregation/STATEMENT.md` §2(i): deterministic,
   6| any partition with |C_b| ≤ B ≤ K, positive tables, **any feasible reference S°**); the proof text of T22(iii)
   7| (`Docs/Theory/proofs/T22iii_T16_start_aggregation/PROOF_v2.tex`, "PROVED-LOCKED CONDITIONAL", reference S₀, EXP′
   8| assumed), cited below as [P:line]; L1 of this folder.
   9| 
  10| ## Statement
  11| 
  12| **Theorem L2.** Assume G; ‖μ‖² ≤ Mn; p ≤ n^A; and (H2) with a deterministic reference S* ∈ Ω, s* = |S*| ≤ v̄ fixed,
  13| s* ≤ K eventually. Let U*_b := S* ∩ C_b and, for p > s*,
  14| 
  15|   u_n := (p − s*)⁻¹ Σ_{l∉S*} max_{T : (b(l),T,l)∈𝓛(S*)} r_{b(l)}(T ∪ {l})/r_{b(l)}(T),
  16|   e_n := 2p max_{b, U⊆C_b : a := |U*_b∖U| > 0} [r_b(U)/r_b(U ∪ U*_b)]^{1/a}
  17| 
  18| (u_n := 0 if p = s*; e_n := 0 on an empty index set). Then with a_n := 2^B √(log n) n^{−κ}:
  19| u_n = O_P(a_n), e_n = o_P(n^{−m}) for every fixed m > 0, and 1 − π₀(S*) = O_P(a_n) → 0. On {π₀(S*) > ½} the
  20| maximiser of γ₀ over Ω is unique and equals S*; hence P(S̃₀ = S*) → 1, whatever the tie rule.
  21| 
  22| ## Proof (substitution list against [P])
  23| 
  24| The proof of [P] uses the truth S₀ only (i) as the reference defining U*_b, the leakage family, u_n, q_n, e_n, and
  25| (ii) through "s₀ fixed, eventually feasible". It never uses μ ∈ span X_{S₀}, nor that leakage indices are nulls, nor
  26| that missing reference variables are true: residual control uses only ‖μ‖² ≤ Mn ([P:149-203]); the leakage integral
  27| allows any δ_{T,l} ([P:249-280]); completion uses VIS only ([P:334-401]). We re-run it with S* in place of S₀:
  28| 
  29| 1. **Setting [P:35-131].** Replace U*_b = S₀ ∩ C_b by U*_b = S* ∩ C_b; 𝓛 := 𝓛(S*) = {(b,T,l) : l ∈ C_b ∖ U*_b,
  30|    U*_b ⊆ T ⊆ C_b ∖ {l}} (note: [P:85] writes l ∉ S₀; here l ∉ S*, which may include true variables — masked truths);
  31|    averages over l ∉ S* with denominator p − s*; VIS (H2b) and E_{T,l}, NL_avg(κ) (H2c)(ii) as in STATEMENT §2.
  32|    The directions u_{T,l} exist for every within-block addition by (H2a) ([P:48-64]).
  33| 2. **EXP′ is proved, not assumed.** Apply L1 to 𝔉_blk := {T : T ⊆ C_b for some b}: |𝔉_blk| ≤ p2^B ≤ 2^{16}n^A
  34|    (fixed J = 16 ≥ B_n, C_F = 2^{16}, D = A, C_V = 2·2^{32}, D_V = 2A), Gram floor by (H2a), 𝒱𝒱 := {r_T} ∪ {r_T − r_{T′}} over 𝔉_blk. L1.3 gives, on 𝒟₁ ∩ 𝒟₂ ∩ 𝒟₃
  35|    (probability → 1) and n ≥ n₀, for every within-block addition (b, T, l):
  36|    log[r_b(T ∪ {l})/r_b(T)] = −½ log(n + 1) − ν log(1 − x_{T,l}) + R_{n,b,T,l}, |R_{n,b,T,l}| ≤ 2κ_E.
  37|    With the remainder defined on the whole space as in L1.3 (R := log[r_b(T+l)/r_b(T)] + ½log(n+1) + ν log(1 − x_{T,l}),
  38|    finite a.s. for n large), ρ_n := max|R| satisfies P(ρ_n > 2κ_E) → 0, so ρ_n = O_P(1): the strict version of
  39|    [P]'s EXP′ ([P:73-80]) holds; the score identity holds a.s. by definition, also off the event.
  40| 3. **Lemma residual [P:149-203]** holds verbatim (it uses only ‖μ‖² ≤ Mn, |𝒯| ≤ p2^B and Gaussian tails).
  41| 4. **Lemma quad [P:205-245]** with NL_C in place of NL_η: on ℋ_n := {max_𝓛 |Z_{T,l}| ≤ h_n} (probability ≥ 1 −
  42|    2^{17}n^{−ε₀}, [P:220-226]), (H2c)(i) gives max_𝓛 (δ_{T,l} + σZ_{T,l})² ≤ σ²(√C_L + √(2(A + ε₀)))² log n; with
  43|    Lemma residual this gives max_𝓛 x_{T,l} = O_P(log n/n), max n x² = o_P(1), and d_n = o_P(1), exactly as in [P:226-243]
  44|    (only "O(log n)" of the numerator was used there; its constant is irrelevant).
  45| 5. **Lemma integral [P:249-280]** is a statement about a single Gaussian and is unchanged.
  46| 6. **Proposition u_n [P:282-329]** holds verbatim with the sums over l ∉ S*, denominator p − s*, and the average
  47|    bound (H2c)(ii) in place of [P]'s (eq:avg); at most 2^B terms per l; Markov; the product bound
  48|    u_n ≤ (n + 1)^{−1/2}exp(ρ_n + d_n)V_n on ℋ_n uses EXP′ (step 2) and step 4. Result: u_n = O_P(a_n).
  49| 7. **Proposition e_n [P:334-401]** with VIS(S*): for (b, U) with a = |U*_b ∖ U| > 0, P := P_{U∪U*_b} − P_U is a
  50|    deterministic projection of rank a (nested subspaces; rank a by (H2a)), 1 ≤ a ≤ B. The telescoping along a fixed
  51|    ordering of the a missing **reference** variables uses EXP′ (step 2); ‖Pμ‖² = g_{b,U} ≥ M_n v_U log n by (H2b);
  52|    [P:368-399] then gives e_n ≤ 2n^A(n + 1)^{1/2}e^{ρ_n}n^{−cM_n/16} on an event of probability → 1, with
  53|    c = σ²/(8C_R), so e_n = o_P(n^{−m}) for every m. (The words "missing true variables" at [P:362] read "missing reference variables" here.)
  54| 8. **Aggregation [P:427-468].** T22(i) with the feasible reference S* (locked; any feasible reference): q_n ≤ u_n and,
  55|    on {u_n < 1}, 1 − π₀(S*) ≤ (s* + 1)u_n/(1 − u_n) + s*e_n. On {u_n ≤ ½}: 1 − π₀(S*) ≤ 2(s* + 1)u_n + s*e_n.
  56|    With s* ≤ v̄ fixed, steps 6–7 give 1 − π₀(S*) = O_P(a_n + e_n) = O_P(a_n) → 0.
  57| 9. **Uniqueness of the mode.** On {π₀(S*) > ½}: every S ∈ Ω ∖ {S*} has π₀(S) ≤ 1 − π₀(S*) < ½ < π₀(S*), i.e.
  58|    γ₀(S) < γ₀(S*). So S* is the unique maximiser of γ₀; any tie rule returns it; under premise e4 the emitted LS0
  59|    centre is S*. Hence P(S̃₀ = S*) ≥ P(π₀(S*) > ½) → 1. ∎
  60| 
  61| **What changed relative to [P], in one list.** Reference S₀ → S*; leakage indices l ∉ S* (may be true variables);
  62| NL_η → (NL_C, NL_avg(κ)) (NL_η implies both for admissible κ and sufficiently small ε₀, [P:404-425]); EXP′ assumed → proved (L1, needs (H2a) and bounded energy);
  63| "s₀ fixed" → "s* ≤ v̄". Nothing else.
  64| 
  65| **Remark (masking).** A masked truth j ∈ C_b ∖ U*_b is a leakage index: (H2c)(i) asks δ²_{T,j} ≤ C_Lσ² log n for
  66| U*_b ⊆ T ⊆ C_b ∖ {j} — at most O(log n) squared partial signal on the leakage family (exact masking, δ = 0, is the
  67| special case η = 0) — while posterior consistency (H0) and the descent
  68| (L3) still recover it. This is the masked regime of M3(f)/M5 in general form.

   1| # L4 — What the production local search does on the event of L3 (deterministic part of (C2))
   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)**; lemma check R04 (Codex Sol): VERIFIED-WITH-AMENDMENTS, amendments
   4| applied (v2). Deterministic, from the search semantics M §6.10
   5| (SoP `02_method.tex:463-467`; LS0: SoP `02_method.tex:490-499`).
   6| 
   7| **Search semantics used (verbatim content of M §6.10, as restated in SoP 02_method.tex:463-467).** From a centre:
   8| scan every feasible flip and swap (additions beyond K excluded), the centre frozen during the scan; every scanned model
   9| is scored; if the best scanned score strictly exceeds the centre's, move there (exact ties among scanned models: the
  10| lexicographically smallest index set) and count one move; at most ℓ moves, then one further scan; stop earlier at the
  11| first scan with no strict improvement (`local_certified`: the returned model is a scanned centre with no improving
  12| neighbour); if the last scan still improves, set `local_limit`. For LS0 the centre is the start mode S̃₀, emitted
  13| (scored) (SoP `02_method.tex:490-494`; premise OP-LS0).
  14| 
  15| The **uncapped greedy path** from C is the sequence C = S⁰, S¹, … where S^{t+1} is the scan-maximiser at S^t (tie rule
  16| as above) if it strictly improves F(S^t), and the path stops otherwise. τ(C) := min{t : S^t = S₀} (∞ if never).
  17| 
  18| **Lemma L4.1.** Suppose the conclusion of Corollary L3.4 holds (for the data at hand) and |𝒱| ≤ min(v̄, K) (if S misses
  19| a truth then |S| ≤ |𝒱| − 1, so the designated truth addition is feasible; extra deletions are always feasible; swaps
  20| preserve size).
  21| Then for every centre C ⊆ 𝒱:
  22| (i) every state S^t of the uncapped path lies in 2^𝒱, F(S⁰) < F(S¹) < …, and τ(C) ≤ 2^{v̄} − 1;
  23| (ii) the uncapped path stops at S₀ (no strict improvement there);
  24| (iii) the capped production search from C performs exactly the scans and moves of the uncapped path up to its cap; it
  25| scores S₀ if ℓ ≥ τ(C) − 1 (if τ(C) = 0, S₀ = C is the emitted centre); and if ℓ ≥ τ(C) the **search endpoint** is
  26| S₀, its completed scan finds no strict improvement (the search certifies its endpoint), and the search does not end at
  27| `local_limit`. (The public flag `local_certified` is evaluated on the finally returned HPM, SoP 02_method.tex:505-506;
  28| it refers to S₀ only when the reported Ŝ⁺ equals this endpoint, e.g. on {π(S₀) > ½}. Not needed for D_n.)
  29| 
  30| *Proof.* (i) Induction: S⁰ = C ⊆ 𝒱. If S^t ⊆ 𝒱 and S^t ≠ S₀, Corollary L3.4 says every maximiser of F over the
  31| feasible neighbours lies in 𝒱 and strictly exceeds F(S^t); the tie rule selects one of these maximisers, so S^{t+1}
  32| exists, S^{t+1} ⊆ 𝒱 and F(S^{t+1}) > F(S^t). Strict monotonicity makes the states pairwise distinct; they lie in
  33| 2^𝒱, which has at most 2^{v̄} elements; the path cannot stop at a state ≠ S₀ (each such state has a strict
  34| improvement) and cannot have more than 2^{v̄} distinct states, so it reaches S₀ after τ(C) ≤ 2^{v̄} − 1 moves.
  35| (ii) By Corollary L3.4, S₀ has no feasible neighbour with F ≥ F(S₀), so the path stops there.
  36| (iii) The capped search and the uncapped path make identical decisions while the move count is below ℓ (same
  37| centres, same scans, same tie rule); the cap only truncates. S₀ = S^{τ} is a scanned neighbour of S^{τ−1}, hence scored
  38| in the scan at S^{τ−1}. That scan is performed iff τ − 1 < ℓ (inside the loop) or τ − 1 = ℓ (the one further scan
  39| after ℓ moves). If ℓ ≥ τ, the τ-th move is made, the centre is S₀, and the next scan (inside the loop if τ < ℓ, else
  40| the final scan) finds no strict improvement by (ii): the search stops with S₀ a scanned centre without improving
  41| neighbour (endpoint certified), and `local_limit` is not set. ∎
  42| 
  43| **Remarks.** (1) Only *centres* stay in 2^𝒱; scanned neighbours outside 𝒱 are scored (and enter the all-scored set),
  44| which is harmless. (2) The bound 2^{v̄} − 1 is crude. A sharper count on LH (Φ(S*) = c moves) needs the separate LH lattice argument
  45| (BS/W4-T38FULL/T38_PROOF.md:217-269, LH-LAT; its own status) and is not claimed here.
  46| (3) Exact ties: the argument holds for any selection among maximisers, because all maximisers lie in 𝒱.
  47| (4) Nothing about the HPM centre of the original final local search is claimed (Lemma 0(b) of W1-T37R: that search
  48| cannot move to S₀ unless F(S₀) exceeds every pre-search score).

   1| # L8 — A canonical, checkable certificate for (H2): block projection coefficients
   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)**. Added after the mid-point review R05 (item 4: "give one worked
   4| non-LH/non-W certificate"; item 2 of the statement lock R01: the exact Λ-minimiser is not a valid certificate in
   5| general). This is a sufficient condition for (H2b)–(H2c); it changes no hypothesis of STATEMENT.md.
   6| 
   7| Setting: fixed design, notation of STATEMENT §1, (H2a) on the actual blocks, and bounded energy ‖μ‖² ≤ Mn with the
   8| same fixed M used in the thresholds below (sweep R10 item 1). Minima over empty supports are +∞ (conditions on blocks
   9| with empty support are vacuous). The certificate supplies (H2b)–(H2c) only; using it in Theorem GEN still requires
  10| S* ⊆ 𝒱, s* ≤ v̄, feasibility and the relevance-set hypothesis (H1) (or S* = S₀). For each block b, since X_{C_b} has full
  11| column rank, the block projection of μ has unique coefficients
  12| 
  13|   P_{C_b}μ = X_{C_b}γ_b,   γ_b ∈ ℝ^{C_b}   (γ_b = G_{C_b}⁻¹X_{C_b}ᵀμ: the regression of μ on the block alone).
  14| 
  15| ## L8.1 Exact certificate
  16| 
  17| **Lemma L8.1.** Let U*_b := supp(γ_b) and S*_can := ∪_b U*_b. Then:
  18| (a) the minimisers of U ↦ Λ_U over U ⊆ C_b are exactly the sets U ⊇ U*_b (so U*_b is the unique ⊆-minimal one);
  19| (b) every leakage residual vanishes: δ_{T,l} = 0 for all (b, T, l) ∈ 𝓛(S*_can) (NL_η with η = 0);
  20| (c) for U ⊆ C_b with U*_b ⊄ U and M := U*_b ∖ U: g_{b,U} ≥ (n − 1)φ₀²‖γ_{b,M}‖² ≥ (n − 1)φ₀² min_{j∈U*_b} γ²_{b,j}.
  21| Hence (H2b) holds for S*_can as soon as the **block beta-min** condition holds:
  22| 
  23|   (n − 1)φ₀² min_{b} min_{j∈supp γ_b} γ²_{b,j} ≥ M_n (σ² + 2M) log n,  M_n → ∞   (empty minima = +∞).      (BBM)
  24| 
  25| *Proof.* For U ⊆ C_b, Λ_U = ‖μ‖² − ‖P_Uμ‖² and ‖P_Uμ‖² = ‖P_U P_{C_b}μ‖² ≤ ‖P_{C_b}μ‖², with equality iff
  26| P_{C_b}μ ∈ span X_U. As X_{C_b} has independent columns, X_{C_b}γ_b ∈ span X_U iff supp(γ_b) ⊆ U. This is (a).
  27| (b) If U*_b ⊆ T ⊆ C_b ∖ {l}, then P_{C_b}μ = X_{U*_b}γ_{b,U*_b} ∈ span X_T, and u_{T,l} ∈ span X_{T∪{l}} ⊆ span X_{C_b}
  28| with u_{T,l} ⊥ span X_T; so δ_{T,l} = u_{T,l}ᵀμ = u_{T,l}ᵀP_{C_b}μ = 0. (c) U ∪ U*_b ⊆ C_b contains supp γ_b, so
  29| P_{U∪U*_b}μ = P_{C_b}μ and (P_{U∪U*_b} − P_U)μ = (I − P_U)P_{C_b}μ = (I − P_U)X_Mγ_{b,M} (the columns in U*_b ∩ U are
  30| annihilated). Its squared norm is γ_{b,M}ᵀ[X_Mᵀ(I − P_U)X_M]γ_{b,M}, and the bracket is the Schur complement of G_U in
  31| G_{U∪M}, with λ_min ≥ (n − 1)φ₀² by (H2a). Finally v_U ≤ σ² + ‖μ‖²/(n − 1) ≤ σ² + Mn/(n − 1) ≤ σ² + 2M for n ≥ 2, so g_{b,U} ≥ M_n v_U log n. ∎
  32| 
  33| ## L8.2 Thresholded certificate (near-zero coefficients)
  34| 
  35| **Lemma L8.2.** Suppose each γ_b splits as γ_b = γ^L_b + γ^S_b with disjoint supports, and for fixed
  36| 0 ≤ η < (√(2A + 1) − √(2A))² and some M_n → ∞:
  37|   (i) ‖X_{C_b}γ^S_b‖² ≤ ησ² log n for every b;
  38|   (ii) √((n − 1)φ₀²) min_{j∈supp γ^L_b}|γ^L_{b,j}| ≥ √(ησ² log n) + √(M_n(σ² + 2M) log n) for every b with
  39|        supp γ^L_b ≠ ∅.
  40| Then S* := ∪_b supp(γ^L_b) satisfies (H2b) and NL_η(S*), hence (H2c).
  41| 
  42| *Proof.* Put U*_b := supp γ^L_b and write P_{C_b}μ = X_{U*_b}γ^L_{b,U*_b} + s_b, s_b := X_{C_b}γ^S_b. For U ⊆ C_b,
  43| projections of μ onto subspaces of span X_{C_b} equal those of P_{C_b}μ. VIS: (P_{U∪U*_b} − P_U)X_{U*_b}γ^L =
  44| (I − P_U)X_Mγ^L_M with norm ≥ √((n − 1)φ₀²)‖γ^L_M‖ (L8.1(c)), and ‖(P_{U∪U*_b} − P_U)s_b‖ ≤ ‖s_b‖ ≤ √(ησ² log n);
  45| so √g_{b,U} ≥ √((n − 1)φ₀²)‖γ^L_M‖ − √(ησ² log n) ≥ √(M_n(σ² + 2M) log n) ≥ √(M_n v_U log n) (n ≥ 2). Leakage: for
  46| U*_b ⊆ T ⊆ C_b ∖ {l}, u_{T,l} ⊥ X_{U*_b}, so δ_{T,l} = u_{T,l}ᵀs_b and δ²_{T,l} ≤ ‖s_b‖² ≤ ησ² log n. ∎
  47| 
  48| ## L8.3 Reading and examples
  49| 
  50| * **Interpretation.** (BBM) is a beta-min condition on the **block-level regression coefficients** of the mean on each
  51|   block's own columns (with the response's full signal, as the tables see it). A true variable is *masked* exactly
  52|   when its block coefficient vanishes (or is negligible, L8.2); a null enters S* exactly when it carries a non-
  53|   negligible block coefficient (a block-level proxy). This is the block analogue of the marginal-correlation condition
  54|   that Song–Liang's Condition 5 imposes globally: here it is imposed per block, and violations (masking) are allowed
  55|   and repaired by the descent (L3) instead of being excluded.
  56| * **Checkability.** Given (X, β, σ², actual partition): one least-squares solve per block (B ≤ 16 columns), then
  57|   (BBM)/(L8.2) are explicit inequalities. For iid designs the population version uses Σ_{C_bC_b}⁻¹Σ_{C_b,·}θ.
  58| * **LH (exact Gram).** γ for an a-group = β_i(1 − ψ_i²)e_{a_i} (only the hub; L6(a)), b-groups γ = 0 (masked), visible
  59|   groups γ = θ_he_h, null groups γ = 0: S*_can = S₀ ∖ M, (BBM) with fixed coefficients. Recovers L6(a)'s (H2).
  60| * **W.** In a signal group C ∋ j₁, P_Cμ = θx_{j₁} + θP_Cx_{j₂}; take γ^L := γ_{j₁}e_{j₁} (the actual coefficient on the
  61|   active coordinate, θ(1 + O(ε_n))) and γ^S := the coefficients on the other coordinates. The off-active part of P_Cμ is
  62|   part of θP_Cx_{j₂}: writing P_Cx_{j₂} = c x_{j₁} + X_{C∖j₁}γ′, X_Cγ^S = θX_{C∖j₁}γ′ = θ(P_Cx_{j₂} − c x_{j₁}), so
  63|   ‖X_Cγ^S‖ ≤ θ(‖P_Cx_{j₂}‖ + |c|√(n − 1)) with ‖P_Cx_{j₂}‖² ≤ (n − 1)·9ε_n²·(4/3) and |c| ≤ (4/3)·3ε_n (λ_min(Σ_C) = ¾,
  64|   ‖Σ_{C,j₂}‖ = 3ε_n); hence ‖X_Cγ^S‖² = O(nθ²ε_n²) → 0;
  65|   null groups: γ^L = 0, ‖X_Cγ^S‖² = ‖P_Cμ‖² = O(nθ²ε_n²). So L8.2(i) holds for any η > 0 eventually. Recovers L6(c).
  66| * **A worked non-LH, non-W instance ("finite-core designs").** Exact Gram; a core 𝒦 of fixed size k̄ ≥ s₀ containing
  67|   S₀ with an arbitrary fixed correlation matrix Σ_𝒦 (λ_min(Σ_𝒦) ≥ φ₀²) and fixed θ; all remaining columns orthogonal to
  68|   𝒦 (arbitrary correlations among themselves, subject to (H0)'s anchored sparse-eigenvalue conditions and (H2a)).
  69|   Then: (H1) holds with 𝒱 := 𝒦, ζ_n = 0 (outside columns are orthogonal to μ and to 𝒦); for any actual partition,
  70|   a block's γ_b is the regression of μ on (C_b ∩ 𝒦) (outside columns in the block get coefficient 0), a fixed
  71|   function of Σ_𝒦, θ and the core's block pattern; if every nonzero entry of every such γ_b is nonzero in the limit
  72|   (generic in (Σ_𝒦, θ)), (BBM) holds with M_n ≍ n/log n and L8.1 gives (H2) with S* = S*_can ⊆ 𝒦. So (C3) holds, with
  73|   masking whenever some truth has zero coefficient in its core block. Example: 𝒦 = {1, 2, 3}, Σ_𝒦 with r₁₂ = r, r₁₃ =
  74|   r₂₃ = 0 (0 < |r| < 1), θ = (1, −r, 0), so μ = x₁ − rx₂ and S₀ = {1, 2}. If 1 and 2 lie in different blocks, the
  75|   block of 2 has γ = 0 on x₂ (Cov(x₂, μ) = r − r = 0, and its other members are orthogonal to μ): x₂ is masked, while
  76|   the block of 1 has γ = (1 − r²)e₁; S*_can = {1}, and the descent adds x₂ (one move). If 1 and 2 share a block,
  77|   γ = (1, −r) on them: no masking, S*_can = S₀. Both cases are covered.

   1| # Lemma CR — elementary sample-correlation tails; consequences [CONC′] and (R′)
   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED (by this seat); XF VERIFIED (R19, Codex gpt-6.1-sol) — v1, 2026-11-08. Note (R19): the complement of
   4| the margin event uses error ≥ δ*; apply [CONC′] at δ ↑ δ* (the bound is continuous in δ). Purpose: (1) a self-contained, explicit replacement for
   5| the classical citation [CONC] (PROOF.md:27-28) used by P2 / P8♯; (2) a fallback for dependency point D2: a summable,
   6| explicit partition-recovery bound that does not use Hotelling's density or W7 Corollary B. Only Laurent–Massart [LM]
   7| and the Gaussian tail are used. NBH = `Theory_work/Old_Projects/New_BVS_Headquarters/`.
   8| 
   9| [LM] (Laurent & Massart 2000, Lemma 1): for k ≥ 1, x > 0, P(χ²_k ≥ k + 2√(kx) + 2x) ≤ e^{−x}, P(χ²_k ≤ k − 2√(kx)) ≤ e^{−x}.
  10| 
  11| ## Lemma CR
  12| Let (u_i, v_i), i ≤ n (n ≥ 3), be iid bivariate normal with correlation r ∈ (−1,1), and r̂ the Pearson sample
  13| correlation (centred, as computed from the standardised Gram matrix; W7 §0.1, `NBH/branch_snapshots/W7-PART/PROOF.md:14-15`).
  14| Then for every δ ∈ (0, 2]:
  15|   P(|r̂ − r| > δ) ≤ 6 exp(−(n−1)δ²/1024).
  16| 
  17| *Proof.* r̂ is invariant under positive affine maps of each coordinate, so take means 0, variances 1, and write
  18| v = ru + sw, s := √(1−r²), with w iid N(0,1) independent of u. Let C be the centring matrix, N := n−1, and
  19| α := ‖Cu‖²/N, β := ‖Cw‖²/N, γ := ⟨Cu, Cw⟩/N, M := [[α, γ], [γ, β]], x := (r, s)ᵀ (‖x‖ = 1), e₁ := (1,0)ᵀ. Since
  20| Cv = rCu + sCw,
  21|   r̂ = e₁ᵀMx / (√(e₁ᵀMe₁) · √(xᵀMx)).
  22| Let η ∈ (0, ¼] and E_η := {|α − 1| ≤ η, |β − 1| ≤ η, |γ| ≤ η}. On E_η, Δ := M − I has entries bounded by η, so
  23| ‖Δ‖_op ≤ ‖Δ‖_F ≤ √(4η²) = 2η ≤ ½ (four entries, each of absolute value ≤ η). Then
  24| |e₁ᵀMx − r| = |e₁ᵀΔx| ≤ 2η, and e₁ᵀMe₁, xᵀMx ∈ [1−2η, 1+2η], so the denominator d ∈ [1−2η, 1+2η]. Hence
  25|   |r̂ − r| ≤ |e₁ᵀMx − r|/d + |r|·|1/d − 1| ≤ 2η/(1−2η) + 2η/(1−2η) ≤ 8η.
  26| Probability of E_ηᶜ: Nα and Nβ are χ²_N. Upper tail with x = Nη²/16: 2√(Nx) + 2x = Nη/2 + Nη²/8 ≤ Nη (η ≤ 1), so
  27| P(α − 1 > η) ≤ e^{−Nη²/16}. Lower tail with x = Nη²/4: P(α − 1 < −η) ≤ e^{−Nη²/4}. Same for β. Given u, Nγ =
  28| ⟨Cu, w⟩ ~ N(0, Nα) (w ⊥ u, ⟨Cu, Cw⟩ = ⟨Cu, w⟩); on {α ≤ 1 + η} ⊆ {α ≤ 2}, P(|Nγ| > Nη | u) ≤ 2e^{−N²η²/(4N)} = 2e^{−Nη²/4}.
  29| So P(E_ηᶜ) ≤ 2(e^{−Nη²/16} + e^{−Nη²/4}) + 2e^{−Nη²/4} ≤ 6e^{−Nη²/16}. With η := δ/8 ≤ ¼:
  30| P(|r̂ − r| > δ) ≤ P(E_ηᶜ) ≤ 6e^{−Nδ²/1024}. ∎
  31| 
  32| ## Corollary [CONC′] (replaces the cited [CONC])
  33| For the LH-iid design (any p, rows iid N(0, Σ), Σ a correlation matrix) and any δ ∈ (0, 2]:
  34|   P(max_{j<k} |r̂_jk − Σ_jk| > δ) ≤ 3p² e^{−(n−1)δ²/1024}.
  35| With p ≤ n^A and δ_n := 32√(2(A+1) log n/(n−1)) (≤ 2 for n ≥ n₀(A)): the bound is ≤ 3n^{2A}n^{−2(A+1)} = 3n^{−2}, summable.
  36| So max_{j<k}|r̂_jk − Σ_jk| ≤ C₁√(log p ∨ log n)/√n-type control holds in the explicit form
  37| max|r̂ − Σ| ≤ δ_n = O(√(log n/n)) w.p. ≥ 1 − 3n^{−2}. *Proof.* Union bound over ≤ p²/2 pairs. ∎
  38| *Use.* P2(a) / P8♯ step 2(a): ‖R̂_T − Σ_T‖_op ≤ |T|·δ_n ≤ L_n δ_n = O((log n)^{3/2}n^{−1/2}) → 0, so λ_min(R̂_T) ≥ λ₀/2 for
  39| all |T| ≤ L_n once L_nδ_n ≤ λ₀/2, on an event of probability ≥ 1 − 3n^{−2}.
  40| 
  41| ## Corollary (R′) (fallback for D2)
  42| On LH-iid with (SIZE) at n: within-group population correlations equal ρ; cross-group ones are 0, ψ_i, ψ_iρ, ψ_iρ²,

params.system:
You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

   1| # L1 — Key lemma U: a uniform, factor-aware bound on the add statistic over ALL subsets
   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)**; key-lemma check R02 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh,
   4| reviews/R02_L1_check_sol.md): VERIFIED-WITH-AMENDMENTS (5 MINOR), all applied — v1.1, 2026-11-09. Falsification
   5| numerics: numerics/fu_check.py → FU_out.txt, fu5_check.py → FU5_out.txt; R02's own exhaustive check (in R02).
   6| 
   7| Notation: STATEMENT.md §1–§2. For a symmetric positive semidefinite p × p matrix M, T ⊆ [p] and l ∉ T with M_TT ≻ 0
   8| and v_M > 0 (R02 item 3; in particular for every positive definite M) put
   9| c_M := M_TT⁻¹M_{Tl} (c_M := 0 if T = ∅), v_M := M_ll − M_{lT}c_M (Schur complement), and the vector
  10| a_M ∈ ℝ^p with (a_M)_l = 1/√v_M, (a_M)_T = −c_M/√v_M, zero elsewhere. For x ∈ ℝ^p,
  11|   Z^M_{T,l}(x) := a_Mᵀx = (x_l − M_{lT}M_TT⁻¹x_T)/√v_M,
  12| the standardised innovation of x_l given x_T when x ~ N(0, M).
  13| 
  14| ## L1.0 The add statistic is a Gram-only innovation
  15| 
  16| Under model G with standardised X (centred columns), R̂ := XᵀX/(n − 1) and g := Xᵀε/(σ√(n − 1)). For T ⊆ [p] with
  17| R̂_TT ≻ 0 and l ∉ T with (I − P_T)x_l ≠ 0, the add direction u_{T,l} := (I − P_T)x_l/‖(I − P_T)x_l‖ satisfies
  18| 
  19|   Z_{T,l} := u_{T,l}ᵀε/σ = Z^{R̂}_{T,l}(g),   and, conditionally on X, g ~ N(0, R̂).                         (0.1)
  20| 
  21| *Proof.* (I − P_T)x_l = x_l − X_T(X_TᵀX_T)⁻¹X_Tᵀx_l, so (I − P_T)x_lᵀε = σ√(n−1)(g_l − R̂_{lT}R̂_TT⁻¹g_T) and
  22| ‖(I − P_T)x_l‖² = (n−1)(R̂_ll − R̂_{lT}R̂_TT⁻¹R̂_{Tl}) = (n−1)v_{R̂}. Since the columns of X are centred, Xᵀε = XᵀCε and
  23| Cov(Xᵀε | X) = σ²XᵀX. ∎
  24| 
  25| So everything below is a statement about a Gaussian vector and its covariance. We avoid a direct union bound over the
  26| innovation normals indexed by (T, l): we union over the local innovation pairs (l, U) and over subsets of factor groups
  27| with thresholds depending on the number of groups (when all groups are singletons the latter are 2^p − 1 subsets, whose
  28| count is absorbed by the size-dependent threshold); the factor variables W_T (up to 2^p of them) are controlled
  29| simultaneously by the deterministic bound U(b), not by counting (R02 item 4).
  30| 
  31| ## L1.1 Exact decomposition along the residual factor direction (one global factor + block-local part)
  32| 
  33| **Lemma U(a).** Let Σ = λλᵀ + Ψ with Ψ ≻ 0 block-diagonal with respect to a partition 𝒢 of [p] (λ arbitrary). On a
  34| probability space carrying independent ξ₀ ~ N(0, 1) and ζ ~ N(0, Ψ), put γ := λξ₀ + ζ (so γ ~ N(0, Σ)). For
  35| T ⊆ [p], l ∉ T, U := T ∩ g(l), define
  36| 
  37|   ψ_{l|U} := Ψ_ll − Ψ_{lU}Ψ_UU⁻¹Ψ_{Ul},   Ξ_{l,U} := (ζ_l − Ψ_{lU}Ψ_UU⁻¹ζ_U)/√ψ_{l|U},
  38|   λ̃_{l|U} := λ_l − Ψ_{lU}Ψ_UU⁻¹λ_U,   s_T := λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹λ_T,   W_T := (ξ₀ − λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹ζ_T)/√(1 + s_T)
  39| 
  40| (empty-set conventions, R02 item 3: only sums/products over empty index sets vanish; explicitly c_∅ = 0, s_∅ = 0,
  41| W_∅ = ξ₀, ψ_{l|∅} = Ψ_ll, λ̃_{l|∅} = λ_l, Ξ_{l,∅} = ζ_l/√Ψ_ll; Ψ_TT⁻¹ is block-diagonal with blocks Ψ_{T_gT_g}⁻¹,
  42| T_g := T ∩ g). Then
  43| Ξ_{l,U} ~ N(0, 1), W_T ~ N(0, 1), Ξ_{l,U} ⊥ W_T (independent), and
  44| 
  45|   Z^Σ_{T,l}(γ) = [√ψ_{l|U} Ξ_{l,U} + (λ̃_{l|U}/√(1 + s_T)) W_T] / √(ψ_{l|U} + λ̃²_{l|U}/(1 + s_T)).          (1.1)
  46| 
  47| *Proof.* Work in L² of the probability space. 𝓗_T := span{γ_j : j ∈ T} ⊆ 𝓚_T := span{ξ₀, ζ_j : j ∈ T}, because
  48| γ_j = λ_jξ₀ + ζ_j. Cov(ξ₀, ζ_T) = diag(1, Ψ_TT) ≻ 0 and Σ_TT ⪰ Ψ_TT ≻ 0, so dim 𝓚_T = |T| + 1 and dim 𝓗_T = |T|;
  49| 𝓚_T ⊖ 𝓗_T is one-dimensional. For jointly Gaussian centred variables the conditional expectation equals the L²
  50| projection, so Z^Σ_{T,l}(γ) = (γ_l − P_{𝓗_T}γ_l)/‖γ_l − P_{𝓗_T}γ_l‖_{L²}. Decompose
  51| 
  52|   γ_l − P_{𝓗_T}γ_l = (γ_l − P_{𝓚_T}γ_l) + (P_{𝓚_T}γ_l − P_{𝓗_T}γ_l),
  53| 
  54| an orthogonal sum (the first term is ⊥ 𝓚_T ⊇ 𝓗_T, the second lies in 𝓚_T ⊖ 𝓗_T).
  55| *First term.* P_{𝓚_T}γ_l = λ_lξ₀ + P_{𝓚_T}ζ_l, and ζ_l is uncorrelated with ξ₀ and with ζ_j for j ∉ g(l) (Ψ block-
  56| diagonal), so P_{𝓚_T}ζ_l = P_{span(ζ_U)}ζ_l = Ψ_{lU}Ψ_UU⁻¹ζ_U. Hence γ_l − P_{𝓚_T}γ_l = ζ_l − Ψ_{lU}Ψ_UU⁻¹ζ_U
  57| = √ψ_{l|U}Ξ_{l,U}, with variance ψ_{l|U} > 0.
  58| *Second term.* Let ω_T := ξ₀ − λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹ζ_T and c := (1 + s_T)⁻¹Ψ_TT⁻¹λ_T. Then cᵀγ_T = (1 + s_T)⁻¹(s_Tξ₀ +
  59| λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹ζ_T) ∈ 𝓗_T and ξ₀ − cᵀγ_T = (1 + s_T)⁻¹ω_T. For j ∈ T, E[ω_Tγ_j] = λ_j − (λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹Ψ_{Tj}) = λ_j − λ_j = 0,
  60| so ω_T ⊥ 𝓗_T, ω_T ∈ 𝓚_T, and ω_T ≠ 0 (Var ω_T = 1 + s_T ≥ 1). Thus 𝓚_T ⊖ 𝓗_T = span(ω_T) and W_T = ω_T/√(1 + s_T)
  61| is its unit vector. The second term is E[γ_lW_T]W_T with
  62|   E[γ_lW_T] = (λ_l − λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹Ψ_{Tl})/√(1 + s_T) = λ̃_{l|U}/√(1 + s_T),
  63| because Ψ_{Tl} vanishes outside U and (Ψ_TT⁻¹λ_T)_U = Ψ_UU⁻¹λ_U (block-diagonality).
  64| *Assembly.* The two terms are orthogonal, so the innovation variance is ψ_{l|U} + λ̃²_{l|U}/(1 + s_T), which gives
  65| (1.1). Ξ_{l,U} ⊥ 𝓚_T ∋ W_T and both are Gaussian, hence independent. ∎
  66| 
  67| **Interpretation (route A).** The innovation of x_l given x_T has an idiosyncratic part, which depends on T only
  68| through T ∩ g(l) (at most p·2^{γ̄−1} distinct standard normals over all (T, l)), and one factor part along the
  69| residual factor variable W_T (one normal per T, shared by all l). This is the "Pythagorean split along the residual
  70| factor direction"; the direction count is controlled by the groups and by k = 1, not by the size of the lattice.
  71| 
  72| ## L1.2 Deterministic bound
  73| 
  74| **Lemma U(b).** In the setting of U(a), let c_min := min{λ_VᵀΨ_VV⁻¹λ_V : ∅ ≠ V ⊆ g ∈ 𝒢} and assume c_min > 0. Put
  75| κ'_{l,U} := |λ̃_{l|U}|/√ψ_{l|U}, κ' := max κ'_{l,U}, κ := κ'/√c_min (= κ(Σ) of STATEMENT §2), and for groups g,
  76| Q_g := ζ_gᵀΨ_gg⁻¹ζ_g. Notation (R02 item 1): κ = κ(λ, Ψ, 𝒢) is representation-dependent; κ'_* := max_{l,U}κ'_{l,U}
  77| = κ√c_min (written κ' below) and κ'_bd := κ̄√c_min ≥ κ'_* whenever κ ≤ κ̄. Note c_min = min_j λ_j²/Ψ_jj (variational
  78| monotonicity with λ in place of ζ) and, in the correlation class, c_min ≤ (1 − ψ₀)/ψ₀, so κ'_bd ≤ κ̄/√ψ₀. For T ≠ ∅
  79| let 𝒢(T) := {g : T ∩ g ≠ ∅}, h_T := |𝒢(T)|. Then for every T ⊆ [p], l ∉ T:
  80| 
  81|   |Z^Σ_{T,l}(γ)| ≤ |Ξ_{l,U}| + κ'|ξ₀|/(1 + s_T) + κ√( Σ_{g∈𝒢(T)} Q_g / h_T )   (the whole last summand is defined
  82|   as 0 if T = ∅).                                                                                              (1.2)
  83| 
  84| *Proof.* Write (1.1) as (αΞ + βW)/√(α² + β²), α = √ψ_{l|U} > 0, β = λ̃_{l|U}/√(1 + s_T). Since √(α² + β²) ≥ α,
  85| |Z| ≤ |Ξ| + (|β|/α)|W| = |Ξ| + κ'_{l,U}|ξ₀ − λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹ζ_T|/(1 + s_T). By block-diagonality,
  86| λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹ζ_T = Σ_{g∈𝒢(T)} λ_{T_g}ᵀΨ_{T_gT_g}⁻¹ζ_{T_g}; by Cauchy–Schwarz in the inner product ⟨x, y⟩ = xᵀΨ_{T_gT_g}⁻¹y,
  87| each summand is at most √(s_{T_g}) √(q_{T_g}) in absolute value, with s_{T_g} := λ_{T_g}ᵀΨ_{T_gT_g}⁻¹λ_{T_g},
  88| q_{T_g} := ζ_{T_g}ᵀΨ_{T_gT_g}⁻¹ζ_{T_g}. Monotonicity: for V ⊆ g, q_V = max_{c∈ℝ^V}(2cᵀζ_V − cᵀΨ_VVc) ≤
  89| max_{c∈ℝ^g}(2cᵀζ_g − cᵀΨ_gg c) = Q_g (extend c by zeros). Cauchy–Schwarz over g and s_T = Σ_g s_{T_g}:
  90| |λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹ζ_T| ≤ √s_T · √(Σ_{𝒢(T)} Q_g). Each nonempty T_g has s_{T_g} ≥ c_min, so s_T ≥ c_min h_T and
  91| √s_T/(1 + s_T) ≤ 1/√s_T ≤ 1/√(c_min h_T). Combine, and use κ'_{l,U}/√c_min ≤ κ. ∎
  92| 
  93| ## L1.3 Probability bounds
  94| 
  95| **Lemma U(c).** In the setting of U(b), let every group have size ≤ γ̄, let G := |𝒢| ≤ p, and fix n ≥ 16 (so
  96| log log n > 0). There is an event E_U(n) with P(E_U(n)ᶜ) ≤ 3/log n on which, for every T ⊆ [p] and l ∉ T,
  97| 
  98|   |Z^Σ_{T,l}(γ)| ≤ √(2 log(p 2^{γ̄}) + 2 log log n) + κ'√(2 log log n) + κ √(a_{h_T})            (1.3)
  99| 
 100| (the whole size-dependent summand is defined as 0 for T = ∅, without evaluating its logarithm), where for 1 ≤ h ≤ G,
 101| with r_h := (2 log(h + 1) + log log n)/h,
 102|   a_h := 2 log(eG/h) + 2r_h + γ̄ + 2√(γ̄ (log(eG/h) + r_h)).
 103| In particular, since G ≤ p and h_T ≥ |T|/γ̄, for T ≠ ∅
 104| 
 105|   √(a_{h_T}) ≤ √(2 log(e γ̄ p/|T|)) + ϱ_n,  ϱ_n := √(2(2 log 2 + log log n) + γ̄ + 2√(γ̄(log(e γ̄ p) + 2 log 2 + log log n))),
 106| 
 107| and ϱ_n = O((log p)^{1/4} + (log log n)^{1/2}); explicitly, with ℓ := log log n ≥ 1 and b := 2 log 2 + ℓ,
 108| ϱ_n ≤ √(2b) + √γ̄ + √2 γ̄^{1/4}[log(eγ̄p) + b]^{1/4} ≤ C(γ̄)[(log p)^{1/4} + ℓ^{1/2}] (n ≥ 16; γ̄ fixed is material).
 109| 
 110| *Proof.* (i) For each (l, U), U ⊆ g(l) ∖ {l}, Ξ_{l,U} ~ N(0, 1); there are at most p2^{γ̄−1} such pairs. With
 111| t² := 2 log(p2^{γ̄−1}) + 2 log log n ≥ 2/π and P(|N(0,1)| > t) ≤ √(2/π)e^{−t²/2}/t ≤ e^{−t²/2}, the union bound gives
 112| P(max|Ξ_{l,U}| > t) ≤ 1/log n; and t ≤ √(2 log(p2^{γ̄}) + 2 log log n).
 113| (ii) P(|ξ₀| > √(2 log log n)) ≤ 1/log n (same tail bound; 2 log log n ≥ 2/π for n ≥ 16).
 114| (iii) The (Q_g)_g are independent (ζ_g independent across groups, Ψ block-diagonal) with Q_g ~ χ²_{|g|}. For a set 𝒥
 115| of h groups, Σ_𝒥 Q_g ~ χ²_D with D ≤ hγ̄. Laurent–Massart (2000, Lemma 1; as cited in PXN lemmas/CR_corr_tails.md):
 116| P(χ²_D ≥ D + 2√(Dx) + 2x) ≤ e^{−x}; the threshold is increasing in D, so it may be replaced by hγ̄ + 2√(hγ̄x) + 2x.
 117| Take x_h := log C(G, h) + 2 log(h + 1) + log log n and union over 𝒥 and h: the failure probability is at most
 118| Σ_{h≥1}(h + 1)^{−2}/log n ≤ 1/log n. On the complement, using log C(G,h) ≤ h log(eG/h),
 119| (1/h)Σ_𝒥 Q_g ≤ γ̄ + 2√(γ̄ x_h/h) + 2x_h/h ≤ a_h.
 120| Let E_U(n) be the intersection of the three events; then (1.2) gives (1.3). For the second display:
 121| √(a + b) ≤ √a + √b with a = 2 log(eG/h), and log(eG/h_T) ≤ log(e γ̄ p/|T|), r_h ≤ 2 log 2 + log log n. ∎
 122| 
 123| ## L1.4 Perturbation: approximate factor Gram (fixed designs) and iid rows
 124| 
 125| **Lemma U(d).** Let Σ ⪰ ψ₀I be a correlation matrix, R a correlation matrix with ‖R − Σ‖_op ≤ δ ≤ ψ₀/4, x ~ N(0, R),
 126| and γ := Σ^{1/2}R^{−1/2}x (so γ ~ N(0, Σ)). Then, for every T ⊆ [p] and l ∉ T,
 127| 
 128|   |Z^R_{T,l}(x) − Z^Σ_{T,l}(γ)| ≤ L_ψ δ ‖x‖,   L_ψ := C₂ + 2C₃/ψ₀,                                               (1.4)
 129| 
 130| with m := 3ψ₀/4, B := m^{−1/2}, C₂ := (1 + B)(3 + B²)/(2m^{3/2}), C₃ := (1 + B)/√m (R02 item 2),
 131| 
 132| and P(‖x‖² > 5(p + 1)u) ≤ e^{−u} for u ≥ 1.
 133| 
 134| *Proof.* λ_min(R) ≥ 3ψ₀/4. For M ∈ {R, Σ}: v_M ≥ λ_min(M) (Schur complement); c_MᵀM_TTc_M ≤ M_ll = 1, so
 135| ‖c_M‖² ≤ 1/λ_min(M) ≤ 4/(3ψ₀). (i) c_R − c_Σ = R_TT⁻¹[(R − Σ)_{Tl} − (R − Σ)_TTc_Σ], so ‖c_R − c_Σ‖ ≤
 136| (4/(3ψ₀))δ(1 + ‖c_Σ‖). (ii) v_M = min_c (e_l − ι_Tc)ᵀM(e_l − ι_Tc) (minimiser c_M), so
 137| v_R ≤ v_Σ + δ(1 + ‖c_Σ‖²) and v_Σ ≤ v_R + δ(1 + ‖c_R‖²): |v_R − v_Σ| ≤ δ(1 + 4/(3ψ₀)). (iii) Hence
 138| ‖a_R − a_Σ‖ ≤ ‖c_R − c_Σ‖/√v_R + (1 + ‖c_Σ‖)·|v_R − v_Σ|/(√(v_Rv_Σ)(√v_R + √v_Σ)) ≤ C₂(ψ₀)δ, and
 139| ‖a_Σ‖ ≤ (1 + ‖c_Σ‖)/√v_Σ ≤ C₃(ψ₀). (iv) ‖x − γ‖ = ‖(R^{1/2} − Σ^{1/2})R^{−1/2}x‖ ≤ ‖R − Σ‖/(√λ_min(R) + √λ_min(Σ)) ·
 140| ‖x‖/√λ_min(R) ≤ (2δ/ψ₀)‖x‖ (for PD A, B: ‖A^{1/2} − B^{1/2}‖ ≤ ‖A − B‖/(√λ_min(A) + √λ_min(B))). (v)
 141| |a_Rᵀx − a_Σᵀγ| ≤ ‖a_R − a_Σ‖‖x‖ + ‖a_Σ‖‖x − γ‖ ≤ (C₂ + 2C₃/ψ₀)δ‖x‖ =: L_ψδ‖x‖. The norm bound: ‖x‖² = wᵀRw with
 142| w ~ N(0, I); Laurent–Massart's weighted form gives P(wᵀRw ≥ tr R + 2√(tr(R²)u) + 2‖R‖u) ≤ e^{−u}; tr R = p,
 143| ‖R‖ ≤ tr R = p, tr R² ≤ ‖R‖ tr R ≤ p², so the threshold is ≤ p + 2p√u + 2pu ≤ 5(p + 1)u for u ≥ 1. ∎
 144| 
 145| Note that ‖Σ‖_op (≈ p λ̄² for a pervasive factor) does not enter L_ψ: only the unit diagonal and λ_min are used.
 146| 
 147| ## L1.5 Consequence used downstream
 148| 
 149| **Corollary U.** Let X satisfy (AG) (STATEMENT §3) with Σ_n ∈ 𝔉(γ̄, ψ₀, κ̄), and let g = Xᵀε/(σ√(n−1)). Let E_n =
 150| E_n(X, ε) be the original-space event that the following inequality holds for every T ⊆ [p] and l ∉ T (with κ' :=
 151| κ'_bd); then P(E_n | X) ≥ 1 − 4/log n on {δ_n ≤ ψ₀/4} (exact Gram: ≥ 1 − 3/log n):
 152| 
 153|   |Z_{T,l}| ≤ √(2 log(p 2^{γ̄}) + 2 log log n) + κ'√(2 log log n) + κ̄ (√(2 log(e γ̄ p/|T|)) + ϱ_n)·1{T ≠ ∅}
 154|             + L_ψ δ_n √(5(p + 1) log log n).
 155| 
 156| *Proof.* (0.1), U(d) with R = R̂, x = g (u = log log n ≥ 1 for n ≥ 16), and U(c) applied to the coupled vector. Fix
 157| X with δ_n ≤ ψ₀/4 and put γ := Σ_n^{1/2}R̂^{−1/2}g. On an enlarged space carrying an independent V ~ N(0, 1), with
 158| b := Σ_n⁻¹λ, set ξ₀ := bᵀγ + √(1 − λᵀΣ_n⁻¹λ)V and ζ := γ − λξ₀ (1 − λᵀΣ_n⁻¹λ > 0 since Ψ ≻ 0). Given X these are
 159| jointly Gaussian with Var ξ₀ = 1, Cov ζ = Ψ, Cov(ξ₀, ζ) = 0, and γ = λξ₀ + ζ exactly; the marginal law of (X, ε) is
 160| unchanged. If A_n is the intersection of the latent U(c) event and the norm event ‖g‖² ≤ 5(p + 1) log log n, then
 161| A_n ⊆ E_n, so P(E_n | X) = P_enl(E_n | X) ≥ P_enl(A_n | X) ≥ 1 − 4/log n. No claim is made that the latent event
 162| belongs to the original σ-field (R02 item 5). Random designs: apply conditionally on X on the design event, then
 163| integrate. ∎
 164| 
 165| Under (AG), L_ψδ_n√(5(p + 1) log log n) → 0.

   1| # L8 — Part III frontier: the path route for exact-Gram compound symmetry (tools proved; target open)
   2| 
   3| Status: Lemma CS-1D and Lemma GAP: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)** (tools; not used by Parts I–II). Conjecture
   4| PATH-CS: **OPEN** (evidence only). Numerics: numerics/cs1d.py (selftest), D2_summary.md, D3_summary.md.
   5| 
   6| ## Lemma CS-1D (exact one-dimensional reduction)
   7| 
   8| Exact Gram XᵀX = (n − 1)[(1 − a)I + a11ᵀ], a ∈ (0, 1), response scaled to yᵀy = n − 1, z := Xᵀy. Put
   9| A := (n + 1)(n − 1)(1 − a) + 1, B := (n + 1)(n − 1)a, A′ := (n − 1)(1 − a) + 1, B′ := (n − 1)a, N_k := k + A/B,
  10| P_T := Σ_{j∈T}z_j², L_T := Σ_{j∈T}z_j. For every T with |T| = k ≤ K,
  11| 
  12|   F(T) = log w(k) + D_k − ν log(0.02 + (n − 1) − (n/A)Φ(T)),   Φ(T) := P_T − L_T²/N_k,
  13|   D_k := −½[(k − 1) log A + log(A + kB) − (k − 1) log A′ − log(A′ + kB′)]  (D_0 := 0), up to the constant log c_n.
  14| 
  15| *Proof.* For |T| = k, G_T = (n − 1)[(1 − a)I_k + a11ᵀ] does not depend on which T; H_T = AI + B11ᵀ,
  16| G_T + I = A′I + B′11ᵀ; det(αI + β11ᵀ) = α^{k−1}(α + kβ) and (αI + β11ᵀ)⁻¹ = α⁻¹(I − β(α + kβ)⁻¹11ᵀ); hence
  17| z_TᵀH_T⁻¹z_T = A⁻¹(P_T − B(A + kB)⁻¹L_T²) = A⁻¹Φ(T) since B/(A + kB) = 1/N_k. Insert into the score of FINAL s1. ∎
  18| (numerics/cs1d.py selftest: agreement with the exact scorer to 5.6e-9 at n = 10⁶; identical LS0 endpoints and move
  19| counts in the selftest — paths themselves were not compared; R06 item 12.)
  20| 
  21| **Move identities (exact).** With c_T := L_T/N_k and N := N_k:
  22|   deletion of e ∈ T:  Φ(T) − Φ(T ∖ e) = (N/(N − 1))(z_e − c_T)²;
  23|   addition of l ∉ T:  Φ(T ∪ l) − Φ(T) = (N/(N + 1))(z_l − c_T)²;
  24|   swap e → l:         Φ(T ∖ e ∪ l) − Φ(T) = u² − v² − (u − v)²/N,  u := z_l − c_T, v := z_e − c_T.
  25| (Elementary algebra from Φ = P − L²/N.) Since F is increasing in Φ at fixed size, the best deletion from T removes the
  26| element of T closest to c_T, the best addition adds the outside element farthest from c_T, and every comparison between
  27| moves reduces to these one-dimensional quantities. For T ⊇ S₀ the signal parts cancel: the null z-values are
  28| z_j = ẑ + τh_j (common ẑ, τ = σ√((n−1)(1−a))/s_Y, h_j iid N(0,1) up to a common shift), truths are displaced by
  29| (n − 1)(1 − a)θ*_j/s_Y, i.e. by order n (order √n in units of τ), and c_T − ẑ is
  30| τ times (Σ_{j∈T}h_j − γ_n)/N with a common γ_n = O_P(1) (L1 U(a) with singleton groups).
  31| 
  32| ## Lemma GAP (deterministic invariant of a deletion path)
  33| 
  34| Suppose LS0 starts at [p] and its first t moves are deletions of nulls, each the element of the current set closest to
  35| its centre c_T. Let D_t be the deleted set. Then (i) D_t is a contiguous run in the order of the null z-values, and
  36| (ii) c_{T_t} lies in the closed interval between the largest kept null below D_t and the smallest kept null above D_t
  37| (with ±∞ if none).
  38| *Proof.* Induction. t = 1: e₁ is the null closest to c_{[p]}; the nearest kept nulls on either side of z_{e₁} are at
  39| least as far from c as z_{e₁}. Step: let e be the kept element closest to c := c_T, say z_e ≥ c (the other case is
  40| symmetric). Then c_{T∖e} = c + (c − z_e)/(N − 1) moves away from z_e by (z_e − c)/(N − 1) < z_e − c ≤ c − ℓ′ (ℓ′ the
  41| nearest kept below; by minimality of e), because N − 1 > 1 (N ≥ s₀ + 1 + A/B > 2 while a null is kept). So the new centre
  42| stays strictly between ℓ′ and the next kept element above z_e; D ∪ {e} is still contiguous. ∎
  43| 
  44| ## Conjecture PATH-CS and where a proof stops
  45| 
  46| **Conjecture PATH-CS.** Exact-Gram CS, fixed a, s₀, θ*, σ², (GC-CS), and the visibility condition making S̃₀ = [p]
  47| (every null has a nonzero conditional factor signal in its block): for every sequence p_n ≤ K (any polynomial growth),
  48| P(LS0 from S̃₀ is a pure deletion path ending at S₀) → 1; in particular D_n → 0.
  49| **Evidence.** D2: exact-Gram simulator, p ∈ {100, 200, 400}, n ∈ {10⁵, 10⁶, 10⁷}: pure deletion paths in every
  50| CS3/CS5/S5/F2 run; F2r p = 200, n = 10⁷: 4/5 pure (one swap); MR1 reached S₀ in every run (D2_summary.md); D3: exact 1-D LS0 from [p], a ∈ {0.3, 0.7, 0.9}, s₀ ∈ {1, 4}, p ∈ {200, 1000},
  51| n ∈ {10⁴, 10⁶, 10⁹} (log p/log n up to 0.75), 720 runs: 720 pure deletion paths, 718 ending at S₀ (D3_summary.md).
  52| **What a proof would need (HEURISTIC outline, not a proved reduction; R06 items 8–10).** With h_k := log w(k) + D_k,
  53| V := 0.02 + n − 1 − (n/A)Φ(T), b := n/A, d := Nδ²/(N − 1) (δ the distance from c_T to the nearest kept null),
  54| a₊ := N max_{l∉T}(z_l − c_T)²/(N + 1) and s₊ := max over swaps of Φ(T ∖ e ∪ l) − Φ(T), the exact gains are
  55| Δ_d = h_{k−1} − h_k − ν log(1 + bd/V), Δ_a = h_{k+1} − h_k − ν log(1 − ba₊/V), Δ_s = −ν log(1 − bs₊/V); the best null
  56| deletion is the chosen move precisely when Δ_d > 0 exceeds Δ_a, Δ_s and the truth-removing gains (tie rule aside). By
  57| Lemma GAP the deleted values lie in the gap containing c_T, so bounding a₊ and s₊ reduces to the balance of the gap
  58| around c_T. While kept nulls remain on both sides, an induction suggests |d₊ − d₋| ≤ (d₊ + d₋)/N + s* (s* a spacing of
  59| consecutive null values), which would make s₊ ≤ (d₊ + d₋)s* — a sketch, not checked. The open case is a late stage in
  60| which all remaining kept nulls lie on one side (m ≥ 2 of them): c_T is pulled towards them and the swap identity gives an
  61| S-gain ≈ 4M²(m − 1)/N (M² ≈ 2 log p) against a deletion gain ≈ log n + M²(1 − r²N/(N − 1)), r := (s₀ + A/B)/N; for large
  62| log p/log n and m ≥ m*(a, s₀) this bound does not exclude a swap. An independent-sign heuristic suggests a scale 2^{−m}
  63| for such endings at fixed m; the probability of these adaptively selected endings is unproved. D3 recorded no swap at
  64| all. Excluding such swaps would establish PATH-CS (pure deletion); controlling a bounded or cap-compatible number of
  65| late swaps would establish only the weaker LS0-discovery conclusion (enough for D_n → 0 via [OP]).
  66| 
  67| ## p > K and k ≥ 2 (not claimed)
  68| * **p > K.** If every variable is visible, S̃₀ has size exactly K; the outside set is then not a gap around the centre,
  69|   and the swap identity predicts improving swaps that bring in outside elements far from c_T, with gain of order
  70|   ρ·2 log p (ρ = n/(n − K) ≈ 2) against a deletion gain ≈ log n. A heuristic count of such swaps is (p − K)·n^{−1/4+o(1)},
  71|   which would exceed the MR1 slack ℓ_n + s₀. Not tested (exact Gram needs p ≤ n − 1 and the regime requires the
  72|   asymptotic start mode); heuristic only.
  73| * **k ≥ 2 global factors.** L1 does not prove a multiple-global-factor theorem. One possible sufficient condition for a
  74|   direct matrix extension of the Cauchy–Schwarz step is a lower bound on λ_min of the T-restricted loading Gram
  75|   proportional to the number of groups hit (with a representation-dependent scale and a treatment of effective rank;
  76|   rank-deficient aligned loadings may reduce to the scalar case). Any obstruction for k ≥ 2 is conjectural.

   8| (|S̃₀| = K) and the first ⌊n^β⌋ moves of the LS0 path are size-preserving swaps (any fixed β < ½), so LS0 with any

  13| ## Proved sufficient change (MR-PK)

  15| path ends at S₀ (a strict local maximum) after at most (1 + δ)|S̃₀| moves, w.p. → 1. Hence **any LS0 cap rule
  16| a ≥ max(ℓ_n, ⌈(1 + δ)|S̃₀|⌉) for a fixed δ > 0** makes LS0 end certified at S₀ (Theorem FAC-PK, (P4)). Candidate rules:

  12| neighbours are the K deletions and the K(p − K) swaps (additions would leave Ω).

  14| ## L2.1 The event E^N_n

  16| * (N1) #{j ∈ [p] : |ξ_j| > 1.5} ≤ 0.14p and Σ_{j∈[p]}|ξ_j| ≤ 0.81p;
  17| * (N2) N_n := #{b ∈ 𝔅 : min_{j∈C_b}ξ_j ≤ −t_n} ≥ n^β.
  18| P(E^N_n) → 1. (N1): Hoeffding for the bounded indicators 1{|ξ_j| > 1.5} (mean 2Φ̄(1.5) = 0.1336) and Bernstein for the
  19| sub-Gaussian |ξ_j| (mean √(2/π) = 0.7979); p → ∞ by (PK). (N2): the block minima of distinct regular blocks are
  20| independent (disjoint coordinates of ξ; 𝔅 is deterministic); each satisfies P(min ≤ −t_n) ≥ Φ̄(t_n) ≥ φ(t_n)/(2t_n)
  21| = n^{−1/2}exp(−17 − 2(log n + 30)^{1/2})/(2t_n√(2π)) =: q_n; |𝔅| ≥ (p − 16(J₀ + s₀))/16 ≥ n/33 for n ≥ n₀ (p > K ≥ (n − 1)/2).

  23| P(Bin < mean/2) ≤ exp(−mean/8) → 0.

  25| ## L2.2 Static scan bounds at size K

  27| (i) every deletion has gain G_del(j) ≤ Δ_K ≤ ½log n + log 3 + 1/K + 4/((n − 1)(1 − ρ)) < ½log n + 1.2;
  28| (ii) if S₀ ⊄ T, some swap has gain ≥ c₃n (c₃ = c₃(ρ, ϑ, σ) > 0);
  29| (iii) if S₀ ⊆ T and some null l ∉ T has ξ_l ≤ −t_n, some swap has gain ≥ ½log n + 2.
  30| Consequently, in cases (ii) and (iii) the best scanned neighbour of T is a swap and strictly increases F.

  33| L0.5(a): Δ_K = log[(2p − K)/K] + ½log(n + 1) + δ_{n,K}; p ≤ n − 1 ≤ 2K + 1 gives (2p − K)/K ≤ 3 + 2/K.
  34| (ii) Pick l ∈ S₀ ∖ T and a null j ∈ T (|T| = K > s₀). By L0.3, G_sw(j, l) = −ν log(1 − nV/(αψ_T)) with
  35| V = t_l² − t_j² − γ_K(t_l − t_j)² = (1 − γ_K)(t_l − t_j)² + 2t_j(t_l − t_j). Here t_l − t_j = z_l − z_j =

  38| t_j = κ_cκ/(K + κ) + κ₁(ξ_j − γ_Ks_T) − γ_Kλ₁ϑ(T ∩ S₀); by L1.1 and (N1) (|s_T| ≤ Σ_{[p]}|ξ| ≤ 0.81(2K + 1)),
  39| |t_j| ≤ C + κ₁(H̄ + 1.7) + C ≤ C√n H̄. Hence V ≥ (1 − γ_K)c₄²n²/4 − 2C√nH̄·Cn ≥ c₄²n²/8, and with α ≤ n², ψ_T ≤ n:
  40| nV/(αψ_T) ≥ c₄²/8 ≥ c₅ := min(c₄²/8, ½) ∈ (0, 1) [R09-E3] (the argument of the log is ψ_{T∖j∪l}/ψ_T ∈ (0, 1)). So G_sw ≥ −ν log(1 − c₅) ≥ (n/2)c₅.

  43| |τ_j| ≤ 3.5. For l: τ_l = ξ_l − x_T ≤ −t_n + 2, so τ_l² ≥ log n + 30, and |τ_l| ≤ H̄ + 2. Then
  44| V_{jl} ≥ (1 − γ_K)τ_l² − 2γ_K|τ_l||τ_j| − (1 + γ_K)τ_j² ≥ log n + 30 − O(log n/K) − 24.6 ≥ log n + 5.

  50| ## L2.3 The first N_n moves are swaps
  51| **Lemma L2.3.** For n ≥ n₀, on E^S_n ∩ E^N_n ∩ 𝒟_n, let C_0 := S̃₀ (any maximiser of γ₀, L1) and C_0, C_1, … the uncapped
  52| §6.10 path. Then its first N_n moves are swaps; in particular |C_i| = K for i ≤ N_n and m* ≥ N_n.

  54| *Proof.* O* := {regular-block minima with ξ ≤ −t_n}: |O*| = N_n and O* ∩ C_0 = ∅ by L1(d). Induction on i < N_n:

  58| ## L2.4 Theorem NEG (claim (P2))
  59| **Theorem NEG.** Under G, (CS), (PK), (PB), (θ) (θ̄ ≠ 0) and the LS0 premises (OP-LS0, e4′, complete scans):
  60| (i) P(LS0(a_n) scores S₀) → 0 for the merged cap a_n = ℓ_n + |S̃₀|, and for the legacy cap ℓ_n;

  62| 
  63| *Proof.* On E^S_n ∩ E^N_n ∩ 𝒟_n (n ≥ n₀): by the single-search prefix property (loop rule (L3) of FINAL `s7_impl.tex`,
  64| valid for every nonnegative integer cap), LS0(a) scans exactly C_0, …, C_{min(a, m*)} of the uncapped path and its
  65| scored set is {C_0} ∪ ⋃_{i ≤ min(a, m*)} N(C_i). Let a be a nonnegative integer with a ≤ K − s₀ − 2 + N_n. For i ≤ min(a, m*), the number of deletions
  66| among the first i moves is ≤ max(0, i − N_n) ≤ K − s₀ − 2 (L2.3), and additions only enlarge, so |C_i| ≥ s₀ + 2; every
  67| member of {C_i} ∪ N(C_i) then has ≥ s₀ + 1 elements, so S₀ is not scored. (ii) follows since |S̃₀| = K (L1(a)) and
  68| N_n ≥ n^β. (i): a_n = ℓ_n + K ≤ K − s₀ − 2 + N_n because N_n ≥ n^β ≥ ℓ_n + s₀ + 2 for n ≥ n₀; ℓ_n ≤ a_n. Finally

   1| # X3 — Deterministic soft-gap lemma for ϖ-approximate argmin deletions
   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)**; lemma check R03 FAILED as written on (iii) (MAJOR) → repaired as R03 proposed;
   4| fresh re-check R03b (Codex Sol high, reviews/R03b_X3_recheck_sol.md): **VERIFIED-WITH-AMENDMENTS**, no FATAL/MAJOR, 3 MINOR
   5| applied (reviews/R03_disposition.md). Falsification numerics: numerics/n3x_softgap.py → N3X_out.txt (random
   6| configurations and adversarial ϖ-approximate choices; the full band containment (viii), the initial-phase bounds
   7| (vii) and the crossing-width consequence of (iii) are checked at every step).
   8| 
   9| This lemma is purely deterministic. It replaces FACB L4.1(i) (exact gap invariant) when the deletion rule is only
  10| approximately the argmin.
  11| 
  12| ## Setting
  13| 
  14| 𝒩 a finite index set with distinct reals (ξ_l)_{l∈𝒩}; constants B ∈ ℝ, κ′ > 1, ϖ ≥ 0. Kept sets
  15| K_0 := 𝒩 ⊋ K_1 ⊋ … ⊋ K_I, K_{i+1} = K_i ∖ {j_i}, |K_i| ≥ 1 for i < I (any length I ≥ 0: every claim is a statement
  16| about this given **prefix** and uses no step beyond I; R02 item 1). Centres
  17| x_i := (Σ_{l∈K_i}ξ_l + B)/(|K_i| + κ′), so that (drift identity) x_{i+1} = x_i − (ξ_{j_i} − x_i)/(|K_i| − 1 + κ′).
  18| Nondegeneracy: ξ_l ≠ x_i for all l, i. **Rule (R_ϖ):** for every i < I,
  19|   |ξ_{j_i} − x_i| ≤ d_i + 2ϖ,  d_i := min_{l∈K_i}|ξ_l − x_i|.
  20| Define a_i := max{ξ_l : l ∈ K_i, ξ_l < x_i} (−∞ if none), b_i := min{ξ_l : l ∈ K_i, ξ_l > x_i} (+∞ if none),
  21| L_i := x_i − a_i, R_i := b_i − x_i, ω_i := b_i − a_i, D_i := 𝒩 ∖ K_i.
  22| (In X4: 𝒩 = 𝒩*, B = Σ_{S₀}ξ − ϱ, κ′ = s₀ + κ, so x_i = x_{T_i}.)
  23|

You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

  76| ## 1. Bounded conditioning preserves exponent alpha
  77| 
  78| **Lemma BC. PROVED (by this seat, unchecked).** For every fixed integer M there
  79| is K_M, uniform in p, positions, indices, and U with |U|<=M, such that
  80| 
  81|     |Cov(W_j,W_k | W_U)| <= K_M (1+d(j,k))^(-alpha), j,k notin U, j!=k.
  82| 
  83| All conditional covariance matrices have spectrum in [c,C], and conditional
  84| variances lie in [c,1], without any size restriction on U.
  85| 
  86| Proof. First take any principal m by m matrix B of Sigma, m<=M+2. Put
  87| K0=max(1,K_dec). Entries are bounded by K0(1+d)^(-alpha), and det B>=c^m.
  88| For i!=j each determinant monomial of the cofactor defining (B^-1)_ij
  89| has a directed path from i to j of length h between 1 and m-1. Indeed a
  90| bijection from rows excluding j to columns excluding i has outdegree one
  91| except at j, indegree one except at i: the component starting at i ends at j;
  92| it cannot join a cycle because that would give a vertex two predecessors.
  93| All other components are cycles. A path edge has distance at least d(i,j)/h
  94| by the triangle inequality. Bound that factor by
  95| K0 (m-1)^alpha (1+d(i,j))^(-alpha) and all remaining factors by K0.
  96| There are (m-1)! monomials. Thus
  97| 
  98|     |(B^-1)_ij| <= (m-1)! K0^(m-1) (m-1)^alpha c^(-m)
  99|                    (1+d(i,j))^(-alpha).                         (P1)
 100| 
 101| This covers m>=2; there is no off-diagonal case for m=1. For
 102| B=Sigma_{U union {j,k}}, the 2 by 2 conditional covariance S is the inverse
 103| of the corresponding principal 2 by 2 submatrix H of B^-1. The eigenvalues
 104| of H are in [1/C,1/c], hence det H>=1/C^2 and
 105| |S_jk|=|H_jk|/det H<=C^2 |H_jk|. Equation (P1) proves BC.
 106| For general U, the Schur complement is the inverse of a principal submatrix
 107| of Sigma^-1, so its spectrum lies in [c,C]; conditional variance is at most
 108| the marginal variance 1. This is the same block-inverse/Rayleigh argument
 109| as `APP/lemmas/L2_CT.md:55`, independent of the decay assumption. QED.
 110| 
 111| Only M=15 is used for sandwich decay, including the conditional covariances
 112| with each truth. The regression on truth residuals in the spherical tail
 113| uses their spectral floor and does not need a new decay estimate conditioned
 114| on the whole truth set.

 116| ## 2. Large-set inverse and regression tails (a different estimate)
 117| 
 118| **Lemma IR. PROVED (by this seat, unchecked).** Suppose A is a principal
 119| submatrix of Sigma on any subset, with original positions retained. For
 120| alpha>2 there is H, uniform in that subset and n, such that
 121| 
 122|     |(A^-1)_ij| <= H f(d(i,j)),
 123|     f(d)=(1+d)^(1-alpha) [log(2+d)]^(alpha-1).                  (P2)
 124| 
 125| Consequently every population regression beta_T(l)=Sigma_TT^-1 Sigma_Tl has
 126| 
 127|     |beta_T(l)_v| <= H f(d(l,v)),
 128|     ||beta_T(l)||_1 <= L0 < infinity,
 129|     sum_{v in T:d(l,v)>r} |beta_T(l)_v| <= F(r)->0.             (P3)
 130| 
 131| Proof. At each positive integer distance there are at most two positions.
 132| Let A_B retain entries at distances <=B, including its diagonal. Schur's
 133| row/column-sum bound gives
 134| 
 135|     ||A-A_B|| <= 2 K_dec sum_{d>B}(1+d)^(-alpha)
 136|               <= H1 B^(1-alpha).
 137| 
 138| For B>=B0, this is <=c/2, so A_B has floor c/2. Fix column j and use
 139| the diagonal weight D_ii=exp(t d(i,j)), t=k/B, with k>0 fixed and small.
 140| The row and column absolute sums of E=D A_B D^-1-A_B are at most
 141| 
 142|     2 K_dec sum_{d=1}^B (1+d)^(-alpha)(exp(td)-1)
 143|     <= 2 K_dec t exp(k) sum_{d>=1} d(1+d)^(-alpha).
 144| 
 145| The series is finite for alpha>2. Choose k so this is <=c/4 for all
 146| B>=1 (decreasing k if necessary). The algebraic part (Schur test + Neumann bound) of
 147| `APP/lemmas/L2_CT.md:22-28` then applies [R06a-1]: (a) the entries of E=D A_B D^-1-A_B are
 148| (A_B)_ik(e^{t(d(i,j)-d(k,j))}-1), bounded via |e^s-1|<=e^{|s|}-1 and |d(i,j)-d(k,j)|<=d(i,k)<=B;
 149| (b) the weight is column-specific, D_ii=e^{t d(i,j)}, so (D A_B^-1 D^-1)_ij=e^{t d(i,j)}(A_B^-1)_ij since
 150| d(j,j)=0; with lambda_min(A_B)>=c/2 and ||E||_2<=c/4, ||(D A_B D^-1)^-1||<=4/c. This gives
 151| 
 152|     |(A_B^-1)_ij| <= (4/c) exp(-k d(i,j)/B).
 153| 
 154| Also the resolvent identity gives
 155| ||A^-1-A_B^-1|| <= (2/c^2)H1 B^(1-alpha). For large d choose
 156| B=floor(d/(M1 log(2+d))), where fixed M1 has k M1>alpha.

 167| L0=2H sum_{d>=1} f(d) and F(r)=2H sum_{d>r} f(d). QED.

 345|     log(p/k)+(1/2)log(n+1)-(1/2)h_{U_b minus {l},l}

 350| partitions and maximizers, using deterministic reference families rather
 351| than a conditional law for a selected partition. If Q=[p], junk exclusion
 352| is vacuous. Equations (P12)-(P15) prove P(Sand_n)->1.

 354| ## 6. NA-R re-run on a polynomial lattice
 355| 
 356| The constant atom l1 bound in `LOC2/lemmas/L4_LOCd.md:51` is insufficient
 357| here: log q can be of order log n. We prove a vanishing l1 bound instead.
 358| Take r_n=ceil(log log(n+exp(exp(1)))), B_l={v!=l:d(v,l)<=r_n},
 359| T'=T intersect B_l. Frames consist of the single functional
 360| r_{T,l}=W_l-E[W_l|W_T']; there are at most p 2^(2r_n) frames and
 361| log N_n<=log p+o(log n). Atoms are the coordinate functionals W_v, v in Q,
 362| each of variance 1. Put lambda_vector=beta_T(l)-zero_padded(beta_T'(l)).
 363| Then e_{T,l}=r_{T,l}-sum_v lambda_v W_v, an exact deterministic row identity.
 364| 
 365| Here is the stronger tail identity. For w in T minus T', write
 366| E[W_w|W_T']=sum_v gamma_{w,v} W_v. Conditional expectation of
 367| E[W_l|W_T] given W_T' equals E[W_l|W_T']; hence the coefficient difference
 368| on T' is minus sum_{w in T minus T'} beta_T(l)_w gamma_w.
 369| The coefficient difference on T minus T' is beta_T(l)_w. Uniqueness of
 370| coefficients follows from the population floor. By (P3), uniformly,
 371| 
 372|     ||lambda_vector||_1
 373|        <= (1+L0) sum_{w in T minus T'} |beta_T(l)_w|
 374|        <= (1+L0) F(r_n) =: L_n ->0.                       (P16)
 375| 
 376| Also D=E[W_l|W_T]-E[W_l|W_T'] has row variance
 377| <=||lambda_vector||_1^2: all covariance entries have absolute value <=1.
 378| The residual e_{T,l} is orthogonal to D, so
 379| 
 380|     Var(r_{T,l})=Var(e_{T,l})+Var(D)
 381|        <=(1+L_n^2/c)Var(e_{T,l}).                         (P17)
 382|

 384| L_n^2(log(q+1)+log log n)=o(log n) and eta_n=L_n^2/c->0.

 402| threshold (`LOC2/lemmas/L2_NAR.md:79`). Neither choice needs an atom-norm event.

 405| zeta_n^2<=2 log p+o(log n), by (P16)-(P17). The sample projection error
 406| in Step 4 (`LOC2/lemmas/L2_NAR.md:96`) is bounded by
 407| 
 408|     epsilon_n <= H6 sqrt(v_n(q+log n)/n)
 409|               =O((q+log n)/sqrt(n)) ->0,                   (P18)

 411| since b<1/2. Its normalization multiplier is 1+O(v_n/n)=1+o(1).

 413| NA threshold is

 416|        >=2log p+(1-2b)log n-O(1).                         (P19)
 417|

 419| tending to one. Finally the reduction

 428| TL, deterministic descent deletes its extras one at a time and the shipped
 429| cap ell_n+|S_tilde_0| exceeds the number of extras. The proof at

 431| and feasibility hold. It gives D_n bounded by the sum of their failure
 432| probabilities. The global population floor supplies LSF; the posterior

 441|    finite-dimensional BC (Section 1). Large-set CD is not invoked.
 442| 2. Exponential regression l1/tail is replaced by IR (Section 2).
 443| 3. Q has radius n^b and q=O(n^b); sample floors use q sqrt(log n/n)->0.
 444|    L0' is re-run with log family size O(q+log n), retaining bounded score
 445|    remainders; the sharp excess requires (q+log n)log n/n->0 (Section 3).
 446| 4. Selection-removal radius becomes n^rho; reference count becomes
 447|    O(n^(15rho)); the recursive correlation error is explicitly re-bounded
 448|    in (P8)-(P9), not claimed to retain the source's faster rate.
 449| 5. The fixed-reference spherical tail is unchanged; its count expectation
 450|    and ladder acquire n^lambda, as (P11)-(P12). The maximum threshold's

 457| 8. TL uses t_n+h_n^2=O(q+log n)=o(n) and fixed beta-min. Descent, cap,
 458|    posterior transfer and output-error assembly need no further changes.
 459| 
 460| Rate audit: (the amended (P13) lower bound tau>1/2 costs nothing, since b<1/4 for alpha>2 [R06a-3].) BC is valid for any alpha>0. IR requires alpha>2. Polynomial
 461| sample floors and (P18) require b<1/2, true for alpha>1. Toolkit, TL,
 462| feasibility require b<1, also true. Selection removal requires
 463| rho>1/(4alpha). The size ladder only requires 15rho<1/2. The strictly

 465| shows feasible rho and tau exist iff alpha>17/2. At equality there is

 467| one fully explicit choice for alpha>17/2 is

 469|     rho = (1/(4alpha) + (1/2-1/(2alpha))/15)/2,
 470|     lambda = 15rho,
 471|     tau = (2lambda + 1-1/alpha)/2.

You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

 146| RSS_A<=C_R n, the RSS lower bound, the table score expansion with remainder difference
 147| <=2 kappa_E, and the nested likelihood lower bound used at G6:371-374.
 148| No lattice-family score event is needed. In particular neither H0, SE_w nor a
 149| posterior assumption is required; claiming all of source L6.2 under the present

 153| ## 4. Selection removal: L6.3
 154| 
 155| [NEW] Fix arbitrary l outside Q and U not containing l, abs(U)<=15. Put

 163| Truths j already in U0 have conditional covariance zero, as does independent noise.

 165| Apply the uniform sample comparisons and evaluate at b=theta*/t. Let z0 be the
 166| sample correlation of W_l,Y given U0, let a,d be their sample partial-correlation

 170|     abs(z0)<=C h_n,   norm(a)+norm(d)<=C h_n,   norm(R^{-1})<=C.

 172| [NEW] The last bound needs no small covariance between v and v' in V. The raw
 173| sample Schur complement of W_V given W_U0 has floor c/2 by the floor on U.

 180|     z_U = (z0-a' R^{-1}d) /

 196| ## 5. Spherical tail: L6.4

 198| [NEW] Fix deterministic l outside Q and U0 in I_l; D=U0 union S0. Regress
 199| W_l on W_D, writing
 200| 
 201|     W_l = W_U0 beta + sum_{j in S0 minus U0} alpha_j (W_j-W_U0 beta_j) + e.

 204| vector with W_l has norm O(n^{-1/2}), so norm(alpha)<=C n^{-1/2}.

 206| N(0,tau^2) entries, c<=tau^2<=1, by FL-R on D union {l}. On the W_D-measurable

 209|     m=(I-P_U0) C sum_j alpha_j (W_j-W_U0 beta_j)

 211| has norm <=C. These replace exactly the AR-specific inputs G6:253-260, as in

 215| fixed, since the true-column scales use only W_D. The projected e is isotropic
 216| in dimension n-1-abs(U0), has norm >=c' sqrt(n) outside an exponentially small
 217| event, and has uniform spherical direction. The bounded m changes sqrt(h) by
 218| at most a constant and a factor 1+O(n^{-1/2}). Consequently uniformly for

 221|     P(E_cov intersect {h_{U0,l}>=t})

 225| tail on CN_D as in G6:291-294. [R04-F1] This conditioning contains t_{S0}; the conditional law of the innovation e
 226| given (W_D, epsilon) is its unconditional N(0, tau^2 I) law, and no law is asserted given a sample-covariance or
 227| scale event. [R04-F4] (2) holds for every 0<=t<=(2A+3)log n with the same proof; the case p=1 is vacuous (Q=[p]). No sphere law after conditioning on sample scales

 243| ## 6. Global size ladder: L6.5 with polylogarithmic Q

 247|     log m(U+l)-log m(U)

 251| family F). Indeed h=O(log n), so
 252| -nu log(1-h/n)=h/2+o(1). Response scaling cancels from RSS ratios (G6:180-185).

 254| [NEW] Here is the ladder including its altered size envelope. For ANY maximizing
 255| S_tilde put k=abs(S_tilde), U_b=S_tilde intersect C_b, k0=q+16s0. A block is
 256| good if it contains all of its truths in U_b; at most s0 blocks are not good.

 263|     k <= k0 + 16 J(t_n(k)).

 275| was chosen. Thus every maximizer, including ties and near-cap sizes, is covered.

 277| ## 7. Truth inclusion, junk exclusion, and feasibility
 278| 
 279| Reuse G6:366-374 verbatim: conditional on X, every Z_{U,j}=u_{U,j}'epsilon/sigma
 280| is N(0,1). There are at most s0 sum_{a<=15}binom(p,a)=n^{O(1)} pairs with
 281| j in S0, j not in U. A normal union bound gives max abs(Z)<=C sqrt(log n)
 282| with probability 1-o(1). Section 3's TV then yields
 283| RSS_U-RSS_{U+j}=(delta_{U,j}+sigma Z_{U,j})^2>=c1 n.
 284| The likelihood lower bound on E_score makes the block-table gain at least
 285| c2 n-(1/2)log(n+1)-2 kappa_E, exceeding prior cost log(2p).
 286| 
 287| [NEW] Every missing truth addition is feasible on (4)'s small-size event.
 288| If Q differs from [p], k<=2k0=2q+32s0<=K-1 by L-feas.
 289| If Q=[p], q<=K<=p forces K=p and any missing truth implies k<p.
 290| Thus an omitted truth strictly improves the start score, contradicting maximality.
 291| This is G6:375-378 and G3:78-84 with the abstract feasibility dichotomy.
